steps.text: Internal energy is the sum of the random kinetic and potential energies of molecules.
First law: ΔU = q + W (energy supplied by heating plus work done on the system).
Isothermal: constant temperature, pV = constant; internal energy unchanged for an ideal gas.
Adiabatic: no heat transfer, so work changes the internal energy; pV^γ = constant.
On a p–V diagram the adiabatic curve is steeper than an isothermal through the same point.
The area under a p–V graph is the work done.
